newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest runoff forecast raised sharply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest runoff forecast raised sharply.

text.p: The Northwest River Forecast Center, in its mid-March update, sharply increased forecasts for spring runoff at hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest, particulary for the lower Columbia River.

The Portland, Ore.-based center, part of the National Weather Service, forecast January-July runoff on the Columbia River at The Dalles dam in Oregon at 140 percent of average, up from an early March forecast of 134 percent.
Last year, runoff at The Dalles, which is the second to last hydropower project on the Columbia, totaled 132 percent of average over the same period.
The January-July inflow forecast for the Lower Granite reservoir on the Snake River in Washington was unchanged at 161 percent of average.
